:knowledge-point/_questions.:knowledge-point/title: Integrating Trigonometric Functions With Linear Arguments

rows.:question/problem:
Evaluate the integral. Give an exact answer.

$$
\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{15 \pi}{16}} \frac{3}{4}\sin\left(\frac{4 x}{3} + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x =
$$

{{answer}}
rows.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=\frac{4 x}{3} + \frac{\pi}{2}.$ Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{4}{3},\qquad \mathrm{d}x=\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\mathrm{d}u.
$$

Transform both bounds using the same substitution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{\pi}{2}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{4}{3}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{7 \pi}{6}\\ x=\frac{15 \pi}{16}&\quad\Longrightarrow\quad u=\frac{4}{3}\left(\frac{15 \pi}{16}\right)+\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{7 \pi}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substitute and integrate:

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{15 \pi}{16}} \frac{3}{4}\sin\left(\frac{4 x}{3} + \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\\ &=\frac{3}{4}\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)\int_{\frac{7 \pi}{6}}^{\frac{7 \pi}{4}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{9}{16}\int_{\frac{7 \pi}{6}}^{\frac{7 \pi}{4}} \sin\left(u\right)\,\mathrm{d}u\\ &=\frac{9}{16}\left[-\cos\left(u\right)\right]_{\frac{7 \pi}{6}}^{\frac{7 \pi}{4}}\\ &=- \frac{9}{16}\left(\cos\left(\frac{7 \pi}{4}\right)-\cos\left(\frac{7 \pi}{6}\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{9}{16}\left(\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-\left(- \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right)\\ &=- \frac{9 \sqrt{3}}{32} - \frac{9 \sqrt{2}}{32}.\end{aligned}
$$
